As Approver, I need to decide. The policy: full_time employees up to write; contractors read or write if advanced training. The Security agent looked up employment type in own database and says contractor with basic security training. Other agents didn't look up employment type except note 1 (HR?) and security.

Actually note 1 (role: Payroll Specialist looked up; employment type: full_time looked up in own database). Note 2 says employment type not looked up. Note 6 security looked up employment type: contractor, and security training: basic.

Conflict in facts. Which to trust? Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and gave specific security training info. The security training detail is unique to security's note. Given contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

Let me think: The evidence supporting decision - Security DB shows contractor, basic training, so max read. Other notes may have outdated info. Since there is a conflict, and security has the most specific/training info, grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
